wa_alpine_lookout_round_mountain_trail.primary: Round Mountain Trail #1529 to Nason Ridge and the lookout spur

why.Merritt Lake trail from the west: For a through-hike of Nason Ridge that starts or ends at Merritt Lake; the lake trail descends about 3.5 miles from the ridge, a much longer trip than the direct climb on the Round Mountain trail.

wa_buckner_mountain_north_face.primary: Boston Basin, Sharkfin Col rappel, and south across the Boston Glacier to the schrund

why.Over Sahale and the Boston-Sahale col fr: To skip the rappel onto the Boston Glacier from Sharkfin Col; the Sahale side is reached from Cascade Pass and camps at Sahale Glacier Camp or the col, but it is a longer way round.

wa_cosho_peak_scramble.primary: Cosho Camp to the 7,830 ft saddle and the north snowfield

why.From Kimtah, down the south gully and th: When linking Cosho with Kimtah in one trip: after Kimtah, a cairned third-class traverse reaches the saddle, so you skip the steep brushy gully up from the Fisher Creek trail.

wa_diamond_in_the_rough.primary: Bedal Creek to the Southwest Face basin

why.Cougar Creek and the North Fork Sauk fro: For a party coming from the north side off FR 49 who accepts a North Fork Sauk ford, a cold Cougar Creek crossing and slide alder; most avoid it and use the Bedal Creek trail.

wa_dumbell_mountain_west.primary: Phelps Creek Trail #1511 to Spider Meadow and upper Phelps Basin

why.Spider Gap from Railroad Creek and Lyman: For parties already doing the Holden Village, Lyman Lake and Spider Gap loop who drop into Phelps Basin from the east; a much longer trip than walking up Phelps Creek.

wa_fortress_mountain_east_ridge.primary: Trinity and the Chiwawa River Trail to the Chiwawa-Fortress col

why.Red Mountain Trail into Chiwawa Basin, t: To reach the Chiwawa-Fortress col from below through the Chiwawa Basin meadows, leaving the river trail early; a good camp option, and the same basin used for Chiwawa Mountain.

wa_mount_angeles_standard.primary: Klahhane Ridge climbers' trail from Hurricane Ridge

why.Switchback Trail up to Klahhane Ridge: To save drive time and the ridge walk: it starts from a small lot lower on the road and climbs about 700 feet in 0.6 mile, steeper than the visitor-centre route, joining the same trail.
why.Heather Park trail from Heart O' the Hil: For a much longer day or a loop, from low on the road and around the west side of the peak; it adds many miles and height compared with the short starts from higher up.

wa_mount_logan_fremont_glacier.primary: Park Creek Pass and the heather traverse to the Fremont saddle and the hogsback

why.Stehekin and the Park Creek trail to Par: To cut the Thunder Creek mileage when the boat and shuttle schedule suits you; fewer miles, but the Lake Chelan ferry, the Stehekin bus and a footlog crossing come with it.

wa_ne_ridge.primary: Upper Cathedral Lake camp, then the grassy south-east slope onto the ridge

why.Cathedral Driveway trail #510A from Loom: When the drive is from the east side via Loomis and Toats Coulee, reaching the same lake basin without the long Andrews Creek valley walk.
why.Thirtymile Trailhead and the Chewuch Riv: When combining the Remmel Lake country with the climb; it is a longer way round than Andrews Creek, starting from the Chewuch River road end.

wa_tenpeak_mountain_southeast.primary: White River Trail #1507 and the old sheep path into Thunder Basin

why.North Fork Sauk Trail, the PCT and Bould: For a multi-day trip through the Napeequa country from the west; far longer, with many stream crossings and brush, so it suits parties wanting a traverse, not a quick trip to the peak.

wa_argonaut_peak_east_ridge.primary: Beverly Turnpike TH over Fourth Creek Pass to Porcupine Creek basin

why.Esmeralda over Longs Pass into Ingalls C: For parties starting from the Teanaway road end who prefer the views; it climbs more than the Ingalls Creek valley walk, crosses Longs Pass and drops about 1,400 feet to the creek.

wa_bread_loaf.primary: Silver Falls loop from the Ohanapecosh side

why.Eastside Trail from the Grove of the Pat: When the campground end of the Silver Falls loop is closed; park at the Grove lot, take the Eastside Trail and return the same way, as the loop cannot be walked through.

wa_emerald_peak_se_ridge.primary: North Fork Entiat to the Pyramid Mountain junction, then the basin between Saska and Emerald

why.Emerald Park and Milham Pass from Lucern: When coming from the Lake Chelan side or linking peaks along the crest; it needs the boat to Lucerne and a long walk up Emerald Park to Milham Pass, and the trail may be closed.

wa_gunrunner.primary: Downey Creek, Bachelor Creek and Itswoot Ridge

why.Stehekin, Agnes Creek and the Blue Glaci: For a trip starting from the Stehekin side; it needs the Lake Chelan boat and park shuttle, then a steep off-trail climb to the Blue Glacier basin on the east side of the peaks.

wa_gunsight_peak_standard.primary: Chickamin Glacier to the snow finger between the main and south spires

why.Stehekin, Agnes Creek and Spruce Creek: When starting from the Stehekin side; the ferry and shuttle logistics are the cost, then a steep off-trail climb from Spruce Creek to a high camp, instead of the Downey Creek route.

wa_liberty_cap_liberty_ridge_finish.primary: White River, St. Elmo Pass and the Carbon Glacier

why.Carbon River and the Wonderland Trail to: Early in the season while the White River road is still closed; it starts lower and is longer, and the Carbon River crossing on the Wonderland Trail can be a problem.

wa_lichtenberg_mountain_se_route.primary: Smithbrook Trail and the crest trail to Lake Valhalla

why.Crest trail north from Stevens Pass: When the gravel Smith Brook road is still under snow or closed, since this start needs no spur road, at the price of a few more miles.

wa_lincoln_peak_standard.primary: Middle Fork Nooksack Road (FR-38) and Rankin Creek to the treeline camp, then the southwest basin

why.Heliotrope Ridge and the Thunder Glacier: When the Middle Fork Nooksack road is closed or washed out; the Heliotrope road is usually open, but expect far more roped glacier travel.

wa_mount_adams_mazama_glacier_headwall.primary: Bird Creek Meadows and Sunrise Camp, on the Yakama Reservation side

why.Cold Springs and the Round the Mountain: When the Bird Creek Meadows side is closed, as it has been in some years, or you are camped on the south side; a longer walk east across the lava flows to reach the same moraine.

wa_mount_adams_mount_adams_circumnavigat.primary: Start and finish at Killen Creek

why.Start and finish at Cold Springs: For a loop from the south-side trailhead, or when you would rather not drive the gravel roads to Killen Creek; it starts with the steep South Climb trail.

wa_mount_baker_cockscomb_ridge.primary: Heliotrope Ridge, the Hogsback and the Coleman-Roosevelt crossing

why.Artist Point and Ptarmigan Ridge to the: When coming at the ridge from the Artist Point side, for example linking it with other Park Glacier objectives; far longer than Heliotrope, and the road there is closed by snow much of the year.

wa_mount_crowder_southwest_route.primary: Hannegan Pass, Easy Ridge and Perfect Pass, then south along the west side of the range to the Phantom-Crowder col

why.Baker River Trail and the Pioneer Ridge: For strong cross-country parties who want the southwest flank from the Baker River trailhead instead of the Chilliwack ford; rarely done, so check the Baker Lake road first.

wa_mount_shuksan_northeast_ridge.primary: Up the North Face to the summit pyramid

why.From the Sulphide Glacier, across the Cr: When you want the ridge as a short outing from the standard Sulphide Glacier route, skipping the North Face; cross the Crystal Glacier to the ridge foot.

wa_mount_stuart_stuart_glacier_couloir.primary: Mountaineer Creek to the basin, then west onto the Stuart Glacier

why.Esmeralda, Ingalls Lake and Stuart Pass: When approaching from the south side, over Ingalls and Stuart Passes to Goat Pass, with a high bivy and a short drop onto the glacier; the northern Mountaineer Creek route is longer.

wa_point_success_south_side.primary: Longmire, the Wonderland Trail and Indian Henry's Hunting Ground

why.Kautz Creek Trail to Indian Henry's: A shorter but steeper way to Indian Henry's than Longmire; the creek crossing is often damaged, and the trail has been reported closed there, so ask about it first.

wa_rock_mountain_west_route.primary: Trail #1587 from US-2 to the Nason Ridge crest

why.Snowy Creek trail from Smith Brook road: For a shorter, gentler and more scenic climb than the steep highway trail; it is north facing, so snow lingers, and the road has had storm damage, so check it is open.

wa_saska_peak_emerald_saska_col.primary: North Fork Entiat and the primitive Pyramid Creek Trail to the Emerald-Saska basin

why.Lake Chelan: Lucerne and Emerald Park to: When you are already on the Lake Chelan side with a boat ride to Lucerne; a long remote approach over Milham Pass instead of the North Fork Entiat road.

wa_silver_star_ne_ridge.primary: SR-20 pullout, Burgundy Creek climbers' trail, the Bench, Burgundy Col

why.Silver Star Creek from the north: In spring on continuous snow, as a ski or snowshoe approach that avoids the steep Burgundy Col slope; longer, and once the valley melts out it turns brushy and swampy.

wa_southeast_ridge_se_corner.primary: Shannon Ridge and the Sulphide Glacier to the notch on the southeast ridge

why.Lake Ann and the Fisher Chimneys to the: When you want to camp at Lake Ann or above the chimneys on a multi-day trip and accept scrambling with rockfall risk; longer and more technical than Shannon Ridge.

wa_sw_ridge.primary: Agnes Creek from High Bridge, into the Blue Glacier basin

why.Downey Creek and the Chickamin Glacier: When starting from the Suiattle River road without the Stehekin boat and shuttle; a long brushy approach, then roped travel over the Chickamin Glacier to the Gunsight peaks.

wa_trapper_mountain_north_couloir.primary: Over the pass at the head of the river road, then east and down to the lake

why.From the valley on the east, reaching th: When coming up from the Stehekin valley by boat instead of crossing the pass; the climb to the lake is off trail, steep and brushy, and the way is not marked.
